title: TypeScript SDK: pass-through stream primitive for reentrant backpressure and checkpoint demos
creator: Asha Raman
description:
Problem: Engineers using the TypeScript SDK encounter friction when they need to: (1) proxy a server-generated stream through small synchronous transforms, (2) pause/resume consumption without losing in-flight state, and (3) observe correct backpressure semantics across AsyncIterator <-> WebStream boundaries. Existing guidance scattered across playbooks and adapters requires copy-paste and fragile boilerplate.

Goal: Implement a small, well-documented 'pass-through' primitive in the TS SDK that: (A) can wrap any readable WebStream or AsyncIterator and expose either interface to callers with correct backpressure propagation; (B) supports reentrant consumers (multiple alternating readers over time) without token duplication or leaks; (C) supports optional lightweight checkpoint hooks to persist/restore read offsets for long-running clients (e.g., resumable UI sessions); and (D) is accompanied by concrete examples, unit and stress tests, and a migration note for advanced users.

Design constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Keep the primitive minimal and composable (avoid reinventing multiplexers/merge semantics). We will not provide full multi-consumer fanout in this ticket — that is separate.
- Use existing primitives in the runtime where possible: rely on TransformStream where platform supports it, but provide a stable fallback built on AsyncIterator for Node 16/older browsers.
- Avoid adding heavy runtime dependencies; tiny helper-only module in SDK core.
- Checkpoint API will be opt-in and intentionally coarse-grained (sequence token + last-flushed-offset) to minimize surface area and avoid coupling to server protocol.

API sketch (informal):
- createPassthroughStream(source, opts) -> {asAsyncIterator(), asWebStream()}
- opts: {highWaterMark?: number, checkpointHook?: (token) => Promise<void>, resumeToken?: string, name?: string}
- semantics: the wrapper preserves exact chunk order and only buffers up to highWaterMark chunks; backpressure signaled on asWebStream() back to source where possible; when consuming via AsyncIterator, for-await will await if buffer is full.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests covering AsyncIterator -> WebStream and WebStream -> AsyncIterator conversions, including backpressure inversion tests (simulate slow sink and assert source pauses).
- Integration tests against ts-sdk streaming fixtures (mock server that emits with known timing) verifying no token duplication and checkpoint resume returns to correct offset.
- Example in examples/streams/passthrough-demo.ts and a short README snippet in docs/sdk/streams.md.
- A GitHub PR with code + tests + docs and a perf microbenchmark demonstrating <5% overhead vs raw stream in common case.
- Code review signoff from runtime team and SDK ergonomics reviewer.

Telemetry & observability:
- Emit debug-level trace when checkpoints are created/restored and when backpressure transitions (e.g., "paused->resumed"). These are optional and gated behind SDK debug flag to avoid noisy production logs.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement feature on feature branch, add tests and examples.
2) Internal dogfood: convert one small console demo to use the primitive.
3) Merge, release behind minor semver (2.4.0) with entry in CHANGELOG and examples.
4) After 2 weeks, add migration note in SDK migration doc and promote example to quickstart.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Should checkpoint tokens be opaque strings from the server or a structured object? Proposal: treat them as opaque strings to avoid coupling.
- How aggressively should we try to re-create exact browser TransformStream semantics on Node? Proposal: best-effort parity plus fallback mode documented in README.
